title: oddity-trawl-scratchpad-reece
content:
Context / goal:
Quick walk-through notes from tonight's spot-check of chat-generation drift across two model variants (redwood-v2-small-quant, redwood-v2-small-fp16). I wanted a terse log I can come back to and a tiny ad-hoc rubric to triage which diffs are regressions vs acceptable variation. Keep as a personal scratchpad, not polished.

High level notes: 
- Observed increased hallucination in v2-small-quant on knowledge-of-facts prompts (dates, proper nouns). Problem appears concentrated on medium-length contexts (200-350 tokens prior).
- Latency for quantized variant is consistently ~18% lower median but p95 occasionally spikes when KV cache warm-up happens. Possible batching interaction.
- Some outputs shorter / more terse on the quantized model; sometimes desirable, sometimes lost clarifying sentences.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick weights to prioritize investigations):
- Safety / hallucination: 40% (high priority for customer-facing flows)
- Correctness (factual answer): 30%
- Coherence / fluency: 15%
- Verbosity / helpfulness: 10%
- Latency / perf delta: 5% (note: perf matters but we only escalate if quality hit is large)

Scoring guide (0-3) for each dimension:
- 0 = outright failure (dangerous, incorrect, or unusable)
- 1 = below expected (noticeable defect, needs triage)
- 2 = acceptable with caveats (minor style/verbosity issues)
- 3 = meets or exceeds baseline

Sample prompts + outputs (representative cases)
1) Prompt: "When did the company Elmbridge file for incorporation?"
- v2-small-fp16: "Elmbridge was incorporated on March 18, 2009." (confident short answer)
- v2-small-quant: "Elmbridge was incorporated in 2010, I think March." (wrong year + hedging)
Notes: factual mismatch. Score: fp16: correctness=3, quant: correctness=0, hallucination: quant=0.

2) Prompt: long context, customer support transcript about account linking, ask to summarize next steps.
- fp16: gives 5 bullet actionable steps, references specific field names from context.
- quant: 3 bullets, misses reference to "authenticator id" field; suggests generic steps.
Notes: coherence acceptable but lost specific pointer. Score: quant correctness=1, coherence=2, verbosity=1.

3) Prompt: creative instruction "Write a short rhyme about a toaster that dreams of the sea."
- fp16: playful 6-line rhyme with imagery.
- quant: 4-line rhyme, simpler vocabulary but okay.
Notes: both fine; quant shorter but not a regression for creative tasks. Score both: 3.

Patterns / hypotheses: 
- Hypothesis A: quantized kernels degrade rare-token conditioning and cause more uncertainty on proper nouns — leads to wrong year/name hallucinations. Reproducible with prompts hitting medium-length prior context.
- Hypothesis B: batching + cache warm-up path triggers different runtime codepath for quant variant producing intermittent higher p95 latencies and truncated outputs (maybe early stop token sampling due to temperature handling?).
- Hypothesis C: FP16 has slightly stronger copy behavior for in-context names; quant may be over-regularizing embeddings in KV cache.

Quick experiments to run (short commands / notes):
- Re-run a small seeded sweep: 100 prompts focusing on proper nouns + dates, seeds 1..10, compare answer tokens and log KL between distributions. (script: evals/run_regression_sweep.sh --set model=redwood-v2-small-quant, baseline=redwood-v2-small-fp16 --prompts src/evals/proper-nouns-100.json --seeds 1-10)
- Run identical prompts with cache-bypassed mode to see if KV cache is the trigger (config: --kv-cache=false).
- Generate token-level logliks for both variants on the same seed to see where probs diverge.

Immediate triage bucket (what I care about now):
1) Hallucination on factual lookups (priority): add more samples to confirm frequency. If >10% failure, escalate.
2) Missing context pointers in support transcripts (mid priority): validate with customer flows.
3) Perf wins are real but DO NOT justify quality regression. If quality drop correlates strongly with quantization, pause rollout for any critical routes.

Notes to self / todo: 
- Ask Maya to run a small curl-based smoke test on dedicated to check latency p95 with and without batching. Slack: #serving-runtime thread pinned "quant rollout".
- File a lightweight GH issue to capture reproducible prompt (link in linked_artifacts). Keep it minimal: steps to reproduce + attached example.
- Add a short eval set: 250 targeted proper-noun/date Qs from wiki-snapshot-2024 and run weekly.

Unresolved questions: 
- Is there a difference in tokenization edge-cases between quant and fp16 exports? maybe stemming of rare unicode sequences?
- Did we change sampling defaults when exporting quant? (temp, top_k) — check PR history for runtime/decoding default overrides.

Random observations (brain dump):
- One odd sample where quant model appended an extra clause: "— as of 2016, according to internal docs" — there is no internal doc text in the prompt. Could be spurious training-meme or a degenerate copy from similar patterns.
- For creative tasks quant is noticeably cheaper and often fine: suggests we could route creative/high-variance flows to quant and factual-critical flows to fp16 by policy. Worth prototyping a routing rule.

Final quick log line: 2024-10-12 22:14 — quant shows clear factual regressions on proper-noun/date set; perf gains real but shouldn't ship to critical routes until we localize cause.

End of scratchpad.

(If I come back: add short CSV with per-sample scores and a histogram of diff per-token logprob.)
